exposure: enrollment in Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program
cohort: The cohort consisted of 80,506 women in New York City who gave birth to a live child in 2018.
finding: The study found that higher socioeconomic status (upper-middle class income) and enrollment in SNAP were associated with higher odds of PCS, while middle-class per capita income categories were associated with lower odds of PCS.
mod_finding: Higher socioeconomic status and enrollment in SNAP were associated with increased odds of primary cesarean section, while certain middle-class income categories were associated with lower odds of primary cesarean section.
